text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvia's Green Party held its seventh congress on Saturday and decided that in coming municipal elections it will run separately from its traditional partner, the Latvian National Conservative Party - LNNK.
- One of the leading government parties, Latvia's Way, also held its congress on Saturday and was criticised by Prime Minister Andris Shkele for a wait-and-see stand and lack of new initiatives.
- The U.N. Development Programme will allocate $3.2 million to help the implementation of the Latvian State Language Programme for the country's large Russian population.
- The head of the Latvia's Way parliamentary faction, Andrej Pantelejev, called for a consolidation of the cabinet, which would mean the government would rely on 55 deputies instead of 80 at present.
- President Guntis Ulmanis left for Lisbon to participate in the OSCE conference there.

- Shkele warned at a press conference on Friday that he would resign if parliament adopted a budget with a deficit. He also rejected proposals which envisage an increase in budget revenues, saying that collecting more taxes is unreal.

- Shkele said that proposals by deputy Janis Adamsons to form a parliamentary committee with a view to investigating the activities of the Latvian Savings Bank and Unibanka undermines the trust of foreign investors in Latvia's banking system.
